title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #453: Prime Products and Squares**

Is it true that for all large n, there exists i < n with p_n² < p_{n+i}·p_{n-i}?

**Answer:** NO.

**History:**
- Erdős-Straus: Conjectured YES
- Selfridge: Conjectured NO
- Pomerance (1979): Proved Selfridge correct

**Key Insight:** Convex hull of (n, log p_n) has infinitely many vertices.

**Status:** SOLVED

mathContext.latex: p_n^2 \stackrel{?}{<} p_{n+i} \cdot p_{n-i} \text{ for some } i < n
mathContext.description: The problem asks whether the square of the n-th prime is always eventually less than the product of symmetric neighbors. Pomerance showed this fails for infinitely many n using convex hull geometry on the prime number graph.

title: The n-th Prime
content:
**nthPrime:**

p_n denotes the n-th prime (1-indexed: p_1=2, p_2=3, ...).

```lean
noncomputable def nthPrime (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0 else Nat.Prime.nthPrime (n - 1)
```

The prime sequence is fundamental to the problem statement.

mathContext.latex: p_n = \text{the } n\text{-th prime}, \quad p_1 = 2,\ p_2 = 3,\ p_3 = 5, \ldots
mathContext.description: 1-indexed prime enumeration using Mathlib's Nat.Prime.nthPrime (0-indexed) with an offset adjustment. Returns 0 for n=0.

title: Erdős-Straus Conjecture
content:
**ErdosStrausConjecture:**

For all large n, there exists i < n with p_n² < p_{n+i}·p_{n-i}.

```lean
def ErdosStrausConjecture : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ i : ℕ, i < n ∧ i > 0 ∧
    (nthPrime n : ℤ) ^ 2 < (nthPrime (n + i) : ℤ) * (nthPrime (n - i) : ℤ)
```

Erdős and Straus originally believed this was true.

mathContext.latex: \exists N,\ \forall n \geq N,\ \exists\, 0 < i < n : p_n^2 < p_{n+i} \cdot p_{n-i}
mathContext.description: The conjecture asserts an eventual universal property: every sufficiently large prime index n admits a symmetric pair whose product exceeds p_n². Cast over ℤ to handle the comparison correctly.

title: Selfridge's Conjecture
content:
**SelfridgeConjecture:**

Infinitely many n have p_n² > p_{n+i}·p_{n-i} for all i < n.

```lean
def SelfridgeConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N,
    ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → i < n →
      (nthPrime n : ℤ) ^ 2 > (nthPrime (n + i) : ℤ) * (nthPrime (n - i) : ℤ)
```

Selfridge disagreed with Erdős-Straus and was proved correct.

mathContext.latex: \forall N,\ \exists n \geq N,\ \forall\, 0 < i < n : p_n^2 > p_{n+i} \cdot p_{n-i}
mathContext.description: Selfridge's counter-conjecture is the negation of Erdős-Straus in a strong form: not just that some n fails, but infinitely many n are 'locally maximal' in the sense that p_n² dominates all symmetric products.

title: Mutually Exclusive
content:
**conjectures_mutually_exclusive:**

The Erdős-Straus and Selfridge conjectures cannot both be true.

```lean
theorem conjectures_mutually_exclusive :
    ErdosStrausConjecture → ¬SelfridgeConjecture
```

If all large n satisfy E-S, there cannot be infinitely many counterexamples.

mathContext.description: Fully proved in Lean by contradiction: if E-S holds from some N, then Selfridge provides an n ≥ N with opposing inequalities, and omega resolves the contradiction on integers.

title: Log-Prime Function
content:
**logPrime:**

a_n = log p_n for the n-th prime.

```lean
noncomputable def logPrime (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  log (nthPrime n)
```

The graph of (n, log p_n) is the prime number graph used in Pomerance's proof.

mathContext.description: The logarithmic transformation converts the multiplicative problem (comparing products of primes) into an additive one (comparing sums of log-primes), enabling convex hull analysis.

title: Ratio Tends to Zero
content:
**logPrime_ratio_tendsto_zero:**

log p_n / n → 0 as n → ∞.

```lean
axiom logPrime_ratio_tendsto_zero :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => logPrime n / n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
```

This follows from PNT: p_n ~ n log n, so log p_n ~ log n + log log n = o(n).

mathContext.description: By PNT, p_n ~ n log n, so log p_n ~ log n + log log n. Both terms are o(n), establishing the sublinearity condition needed for the convex hull lemma.

title: Convex Hull Vertex
content:
**IsConvexHullVertex:**

A point (n, a_n) is on the upper convex hull boundary if 2·a_n > a_{n-i} + a_{n+i} for all i.

```lean
def IsConvexHullVertex (a : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → i < n → 2 * a n > a (n - i) + a (n + i)
```

At a vertex, the point lies above the line between neighbors.

mathContext.description: A discrete analogue of strict concavity at a point. The condition means (n, a_n) lies strictly above the midpoint of the chord from (n-i, a_{n-i}) to (n+i, a_{n+i}), characterizing vertices of the upper convex hull.

title: Pomerance's Lemma
content:
**pomerance_convex_hull_lemma:**

For any sequence with a_n = o(n), there are infinitely many convex hull vertices.

```lean
axiom pomerance_convex_hull_lemma (a : ℕ → ℝ)
    (h : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => a n / n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, IsConvexHullVertex a n
```

The non-horizontal boundary is concave with infinitely many vertices.

mathContext.latex: a_n = o(n) \Rightarrow \text{infinitely many } n \text{ are convex hull vertices}
mathContext.description: The key geometric insight: if a sequence grows sublinearly, the upper convex hull of (n, a_n) has a non-horizontal boundary that is concave, forcing infinitely many points to be genuine vertices (not interior to any edge).

title: Pomerance (1979)
content:
**pomerance_1979:**

Infinitely many n have p_n² > p_{n+i}·p_{n-i} for all i < n.

```lean
axiom pomerance_1979 :
    ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N,
      ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → i < n →
        (nthPrime n : ℤ) ^ 2 > (nthPrime (n + i) : ℤ) * (nthPrime (n - i) : ℤ)
```

Published in 'The prime number graph', Math. Comp. (1979).

mathContext.latex: \forall N,\ \exists n \geq N,\ \forall\, 0 < i < n : p_n^2 > p_{n+i} \cdot p_{n-i}
mathContext.description: Pomerance's main theorem, combining the convex hull lemma (applied to a_n = log p_n with the PNT sublinearity condition) with the log-to-product exponentiation step.

title: Selfridge Was Correct
content:
**selfridge_correct:**

Selfridge's conjecture is true.

```lean
theorem selfridge_correct : SelfridgeConjecture := pomerance_1979
```

Direct application of Pomerance's result.

mathContext.description: Pomerance's theorem is definitionally equal to Selfridge's conjecture, so the proof is a direct term-level assignment — no tactics needed.

title: Erdős-Straus Were Wrong
content:
**erdos_straus_wrong:**

The Erdős-Straus conjecture is false.

```lean
theorem erdos_straus_wrong : ¬ErdosStrausConjecture := by
  intro hES
  exact conjectures_mutually_exclusive hES selfridge_correct
```

Follows from mutual exclusivity and Selfridge being correct.

mathContext.description: A two-step proof: assume E-S, apply mutual exclusivity to get ¬Selfridge, contradicting selfridge_correct. This chain (Pomerance → Selfridge → ¬E-S) is the complete logical structure.

title: Erdős Problem #453: SOLVED
content:
**erdos_453_solution:**

The answer to Problem #453 is NO.

```lean
theorem erdos_453_solution : ¬ErdosStrausConjecture :=
  erdos_straus_wrong
```

It is NOT true that for all large n, some i exists with p_n² < p_{n+i}·p_{n-i}.

mathContext.latex: \neg\bigl(\exists N,\ \forall n \geq N,\ \exists\, 0 < i < n : p_n^2 < p_{n+i} p_{n-i}\bigr)
mathContext.description: The final answer to Problem #453, delegating to erdos_straus_wrong. The answer is definitively NO — the Erdős-Straus conjecture is false.

title: Summary
content:
**erdos_453_summary:**

Combines the main results.

```lean
theorem erdos_453_summary :
    ¬ErdosStrausConjecture ∧ SelfridgeConjecture
```

**Key Results:**
1. Erdős-Straus conjecture is FALSE
2. Selfridge's counter-conjecture is TRUE
3. Pomerance's proof uses convex hull geometry
4. Problem A14 in Guy's UPINT

**Status:** SOLVED

mathContext.description: The conjunction packages both halves of the resolution: the original conjecture is false AND the counter-conjecture is true. Proved by the pair ⟨erdos_straus_wrong, selfridge_correct⟩.
